headline: Ad softness, higher costs squeeze profit despite VAS gains
summary_short: Weibo's Q2 FY2026 net revenues rose 2% y/y to $453.8 million as 19% VAS growth offset a 1% dip in advertising, but net income attributable to shareholders fell 46% y/y to $67.4 million ($0.26 diluted GAAP EPS) on higher costs and an investment fair-value loss.
summary_long: Net revenues were $453.8M, up 2% y/y (down 4% on a constant-currency basis), as VAS revenue grew 19% to $72.9M on one-off ticket proceeds and membership growth, while advertising and marketing revenue fell 1% to $381.0M on softer demand from handset and online-game advertisers, partly offset by internet-service and automobile spend and favorable FX. Costs and expenses rose 12% to $335.0M on higher ad-production and marketing spend, compressing operating margin to 26% from 33% a year ago. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.38, down from $0.54, as a $22.8M investment fair-value loss dragged net income to $67.4M. Cash, equivalents and short-term investments totaled $2.64B. No forward guidance was issued.
confidence_notes: Resolver-supplied eps_usd prior_yy (0.53, Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries) differs slightly from the release's own stated Q2 2025 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.54; the eps_usd KPI row above uses the resolver's ledger value per the same-basis rule, while summary_long cites the release's own $0.54 figure directly -- both are noted here rather than reconciled by guesswork. 'Revenue' is Weibo's own reported total net revenues (advertising + marketing plus VAS), not a Yahoo aggregate. Operating margin (26% vs 33%) is stated verbatim by the company, not computed on the shard. No guidance section appears in this release -- Weibo did not issue forward guidance for Q3 or FY2026.

drivers.explanation: Decline reflects softer advertiser demand from handset and online-game sectors, partly offset by higher internet-service and automobile spend and favorable RMB appreciation on reported figures.
Growth driven by one-off ticket proceeds from offline activities, solid membership-service growth, and favorable foreign-exchange impact on reported numbers.
Margin compression driven by a 12% rise in costs and expenses, mainly higher ad-production costs and marketing expenses.
Decline driven by a $27.8M non-operating loss (vs $12.8M non-operating income a year ago), including a $22.8M investment fair-value loss, on top of the margin compression.
CEO Gaofei Wang called it "a solid quarter," citing improved user engagement, higher video consumption from the revamped feed, and progress integrating AI across product, content and monetization.
